LESSON: LINEAR INEQUALITIES

Grade: Grade 7
Subject: MATHEMATICS
Strand: Algebra 2.2 Linear Equations (6 lessons) Forming and solving linear equations By
Topic 2.3: Linear Inequalities
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 8

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Linear Inequalities, part of Algebra 2.2 Linear Equations (6 lessons) Forming and solving linear equations By in Grade 7 MATHEMATICS.

Key inquiry question: How do we use linear inequalities in real-life? 2. Why do we use linear inequalities in real-life?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

A. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. use inequality cards to complete simple inequality statements using symbols

2. use inequality cards/objects to form simple linear inequalities with one unknown

3. draw and represent simple inequality statements on a number line

4. use inequality cards to complete compound inequality statements. Have examples that may involve gender such as the number of boys and girls in class

5. draw and represent compound inequality statements on a number line

6. use IT devices in graphing tools to present solutions to inequalities. 1.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. use inequality cards to complete simple inequality statements using symbols
2. use inequality cards/objects to form simple linear inequalities with one unknown
3. draw and represent simple inequality statements on a number line
4. use inequality cards to complete compound inequality statements. Have examples that may involve gender such as the number of boys and girls in class
5. draw and represent compound inequality statements on a number line
6. use IT devices in graphing tools to present solutions to inequalities. 1.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Linear Inequalities together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and Collaboration: as the learner discusses how to form linear inequalities.

● Creativity and Imagination: as the learner draws and represents inequality statements on a number line.

Values

Integrity: as the learner observes and adheres to the conditions of the given inequalities.
